value.get_item: get_item(sku: str) -> dict | None. Returns {"sku": str, "name": str, "price": float (dollars, 12.5 means $12.50), "category": str}, or None if the sku is unknown.
value.get_customer: get_customer(customer_id: str) -> dict | None. Returns {"id": str, "name": str, "discount": float (fraction, 0.10 means 10%), "region": str (e.g. "TX")}, or None if unknown.
value.notes: pricing.py supplies data only; it does not compute tax or totals. Ids and skus are case-sensitive strings. Money is float dollars; percentages are fractions.

why: Defines the pricing->tax/invoice API. tax.py needs customer region; invoice.py needs item price, name and customer discount. Team standard: money as float dollars, percentages as fractions, not-found returns None.

args.region: str or null: customer region code, e.g. "TX"; null = unknown customer
args.lines: list of [category:str, amount_cents:int] for ALL order lines before discount; tax.py decides exemption

compute_tax.returns: int cents: tax amount only, not the total

tax_rate_pct.returns: Decimal percent, e.g. Decimal("8.25"); null region -> Decimal(0)

value.errors: unknown non-null region (not in rates.csv) raises KeyError

why: Keeps all tax rules in tax.py; invoice only passes region, line categories/amounts, discount. Integer cents in and out, percent numbers, KeyError on unknown region per team standard.

value.unknown_customer: region == null (no customer record) -> 0% tax, no error
value.OR: OR is listed in rates.csv with 0, so it is a normal lookup and not an unknown customer

why: RULES.md says an unknown customer pays 0%, but team standard says failed lookups raise KeyError. Resolving: the null region case is handled explicitly as unknown customer; a region string that is not in rates.csv is a real lookup failure and raises KeyError.

value.is_known_sku: pricing.is_known_sku(sku) -> bool (needed because unit_price 0 is ambiguous with a free item)
value.customer_name: pricing.customer_name(customer_id) -> str; empty string if unknown
value.discount_multiplier: pricing.discount_multiplier(customer_id) -> Decimal; 0.90 for 10% off; Decimal(1) if unknown customer

why: Interface agent1 provides to invoice.py. Follows team standard (defaults on miss, multipliers, Decimal). is_known_sku separates unknown SKUs from free items, which the default-0 rule cannot.

value.calculate: tax.calculate(customer_id, lines, discount) -> (rate_multiplier: Decimal, tax_amount: Decimal rounded to cent half-up). lines = list of (sku, line_amount Decimal) for KNOWN skus only, before discount. discount = invoice discount Decimal dollars (already rounded to cent by invoice.py). tax.py decides taxability per sku and applies the discount to the taxable base. Unknown customer: (Decimal(1), Decimal(0)).
